newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cabinet passes reform of pensions system.
newsitem.headline: German cabinet passes reform of pensions system.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet on Wednesday approved a draft law designed to reform the German pensions system to take account of the ageing of the country's population.

The bill, drafted by Labour Minister Norbert Bluem, outlines a step-by-step plan to cut a typical pension to 64 percent of average net wages from around 70 percent now. The reduction is due to be phased in from 1999.
"The reform of the pensions system agreed by the cabinet today guarantees a fair balance between the generations," said Peter Hintze, general secretary of Kohl's Christian Democrats.
"Norbert Bluem has presented a concept which takes full account of the changes in the age structure of the population."

The opposition Social Democrats (SPD) reiterated their opposition to the plan, saying it was socially unjust and did not address fundamental problems. They pledged to put the issue at the centre of their 1998 general election campaign.
